items: **Capital:** Vijayapuri; its modern name is Nagarjuna Konda.
**Gold coins by Santamula-I:** issued crores of gold coins.
**Virapurushadatta:** popular Ikshvaku king; Buddhism flourished in his reign, the Golden age of Buddhism.
**Upasika Bodhisri** contributed to Buddhism during the reign of Virapurushadatta.
**Inscriptions of Vasisthiputra Santamula:** recently discovered in Rentala and Kesavapath.
Multiple gifts to different sections & institutions
Important evidence of Buddhism patronage under Ikshvakus
Found near Vijayapuri; similar to Nagarjunakonda
**Prakrit:** the inscriptional language of the Ikshvaku period; the early inscriptions are in Prakrit.

parts.t: Deities and temples of Nagarjuna Konda
items: **Temple architecture:** initiated during the Ikshvaku period.
Constructed by the Ikshvaku Commander Elisiri for Kumara Swami
Temple located here; Abhira / Ikshvaku period
**Temples discovered in excavations near Nagarjuna Konda:** Harati, Mahajana, Kumara Swami, Pushpabhadra Swami, Ashtabhoji Narayana Swami.
**Motupalli:** important port of the Ikshvaku period (along with Ghantasala).
**Ghantasala:** important Ikshvaku port; mentioned by the Alexandrian geographer Claudius Ptolemy as the maritime emporium Kantakossyla (Krishna district).
**Nigamalu:** trade guilds during the Ikshvaku period.
**Koduru:** ancient name of present Gudur (Bandar taluk, Krishna).
**Feudatories:** the Brihatpalayanas were feudatories of the Ikshvakus (Nagarjunakonda inscription, Ikshvaku Dynasty).
**Pantur village:** granted to Eight Brahmins (Jayavarma period).
The **Kondamudi Copper Edict** is the only inscription about the Brihatpalayanas.
**Issued by:** Jayavarma (Brihatpalayana), in the 10th year of his reign; it mentions Jayavarma.
**Pallavas:** responsible for the rise of Brahmanism & the downfall of Buddhism.

parts.t: The Salankayanas: founder, capital and kings
items: **Founder of the Salankayana Dynasty:** Vijaya Deva Varma.
**Capital:** Vengipuram; its present name is Pedavegi (near Eluru, West Godavari).
**Hastivarma (Salankayana):** contemporary of Samudragupta; the Allahabad Pillar inscription of Samudragupta mentions Hastivarma.
Grant of land to Vishnu; 1st to mention Vishnu temples in Andhra
**Prakrit:** 3 of the 8 Salankayana inscriptions are in Prakrit.
**Sanskrit:** replaced Prakrit as official language from the Salankayanas onwards; 5 of 8 Salankayana inscriptions are in Sanskrit.
**Chitraratha Swamy:** family deity of the Salankayanas (means Sun).
**Bappa Bhattaraka:** the Salankayanas declared themselves as devotees; it means "consideration of father as God".
**Vishnu:** land grant to Vishnu mentioned in the Pedavegi inscription (Nandi Varma-II).

lectures.title: Medieval Andhra: Palnadu, Musunuri Nayakas, trade and terms

items: **Battle of Palnadu / Palanadu (1182):** Nagamma was responsible; Kakati Rudra Deva helped Nalagama Raju.
**Chapa Koodu / Dasa Samaj:** by Brahma Nayudu (Brahma Naidu), c.1170–1182 CE, in Palnadu; inter-caste dining.
**Dasa Samaj:** established in Andhra by Brahma Naidu.
**Pithapuram inscription:** of Prithvisvara of Velanadu; mentions Kolleru lake.
**Liberation Movement (post-Kakatiya):** Prolaya Nayaka was the leader of the confederacy.
**Machilipatnam / Masulipatnam (Golconda, 16-17th cent.):** most famous port for textile trade; famous for diamonds trade (1600s).
**Tavernier:** 17th century trader who visited Andhra mines for best quality precious stones & diamonds.
**Kohinoor Diamond:** discovered in the diamond mines at Kolluru.
**Itsing:** Chinese traveller of the Post-Satavahana Era; saw students by-hearting "Sushrullekha" in India.
**Founder of Hyderabad City:** Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah.
Guild formed by Agriculturists (Medieval Deccan & South India)
Advisor to the king in Judiciary (Ancient / Medieval)
Tax on trade and occupations / looms
Officials who enjoyed land without cess/tax (Number = 12)
**Sriparvata Swamy:** associated with the Vishnukundins; identified with Buddha by N. Venkata Ramanaiah.
**Vasavi:** goddess of the Arya Vysya Community; the main seat of the goddess Vasavi was Penugonda.
**Earliest inscriptions relating to AP history:** in Prakrit language.
**First inscription in Telugu:** the Kalamalla inscription, of Erikal Mutthuraju Dhananjaya Varma.
**First World Telugu Conference:** first held in 1975 (to encourage Telugu language, literature & culture).
**AP Sahitya Academy (Andhra Pradesh Sahitya Academy):** Govt. AP, 1957; Telugu literature; manuscripts + lexicons.
**History of Ancient India & History of South India**
**Asamarthuni Jeevitha Yatra:** novel by T. Gopichand, 1947; celebrated as the first psychological novel in Telugu literature.
**Sangita Sudhakaram (Sangita-Sudhakaram):** work on music composed by Singabhupala II (Singa Bhupala II).
**Yenki songs:** author Nanduri Subba Rao (in Telugu).

lectures.title: Temples, caves, art and old place names of Andhra

items: **Bhairavakonda Caves:** Nellore district; number of caves = Eight; Centre of Saivism.
**Ajanta Cave No. 10:** the "Swetagaja Jataka" painting can be seen here.
Present name: Pedavegi (near Eluru, West Godavari)
Ancient name of present Gudur (Bandar taluk, Krishna)
Father of Modern Economics; Father of Capitalism
Pure Monetary Theory of Trade Cycle
**Amartya Sen:** Welfare economics + Social Choice Theory.
**Bina Agarwal:** Indian economist; Leontief Award for 2009-10 (announced in 2009, presented in 2010).
Pure Monetary Theory of Trade Cycle
**On the Principles of Political Economy and Taxation**
**The General Theory of Employment, Interest and Money**

items: **Kelkar Committee:** chairman Vijay L. Kelkar; PPP Infrastructure Model.
